1.6.3. PrimeTime League – Gender doubles, aged 65+ scheduled play on Fridays

5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

6.2.3. Match Day Format: (See table below)
6.2.3.1. All Games: Games to 15 using Rally Scoring* (win by 1). 1 point per win. Two
one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams
switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points. Visitors choose serve,
receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.
6.2.3.2. Men's Round Robin: 3 Men’s teams play Round Robin (from low to high,
Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.3. Women's Round Robin: 3 Women’s teams play Round Robin (from low to
high, Teams 4 to 6). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.
6.2.3.5. Picklebreaker™ Game (Only played if tie at the end of all previous rounds -
12-12): Features all the mixed teams that played in the Mixed rounds. This will

be one game to 25 win by 2 using Rally Scoring. The winning team collects 3
additional points. (If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 3-point
bonus.) Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not
reflect on individual’s W/L record.
Teams are numbered 1–3 for Men’s Doubles, 4–6 for Women’s Doubles, and 7–12 for Mixed
Doubles. These team numbers correspond directly to the Match Score Sheet printed from the system.
We highly recommend assigning higher team numbers to teams with higher combined skill levels and
ratings (for instance, Team 6 should have a higher combined DUPR rating than Team 4 in Women’s or
Team 12 should be a higher team rating than Team 7 in Mixed Doubles).

6.2.4. Scoring: A maximum of 27 total possible match points per date. This includes 24
possible points awarded during standard play, plus a 3-point bonus. If the match
ends in a tie after the mixed doubles division (12-12), a Picklebreaker will be played
to determine the winner of the 3 bonus points. If there is no tie, the leading team
automatically receives the 3-point bonus.

6.2.5. Player Cap: Every player plays 3 gender double games to 15 and will then play 1
mixed game to 15. Optional lineups may include players who compete only in
gender doubles or only in mixed doubles. Depending on the outcome, the 6 mixed
teams will then play the Picklebreaker sequence playing up to 4+ points per team.

rows.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Double Elimination
rows.content:
15.B.1 Double Elimination. In a double elimination format, after losing
one match, a singles player or doubles team plays in a consolation
bracket. The player or team is eliminated from competition after
one loss in the consolation bracket. The winner of the consolation
bracket plays the winner of the winners’ bracket to determine first
place and second place. If the winner of the consolation bracket
defeats the winner of the winners’ bracket, then a tie-breaker
match to 15 points must be played to determine first place and
second place. The loser of the final match in the consolation
bracket wins third place.

rows.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Single Elimination with Consolation
rows.content:
15.B.2 Single Elimination with Consolation. In a single elimination with
consolation format, after losing one match, a singles player or
doubles team plays in a consolation bracket. The player or team is
eliminated from competition after one loss in the consolation
bracket. The final two players or teams in the winners’ bracket play
for first place and second place. The final two singles players or
doubles teams in the consolation bracket play for third place.

Appendix B Rulebook Priorities and Guiding
Principles
Preface
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook is the organization’s most important product.
It is the foundational document for the sport of pickleball and should be treated
with the respect accorded the sport’s founders and those who have written and
approved rules over the years.
Writing rules that are objective, clear, and concise is difficult work. Because those
involved in writing and/or approving rules come from diverse backgrounds and
experiences, it is important to have rule writing priorities and guiding principles
that help provide a measure of consistency from year to year. The following
Rulebook Priorities and Guiding Principles were developed to guide rule writers and
approvers in their important work.
Priorities
The following three priorities should be considered “tests” for any suggested rule
change. Any suggested rule change should satisfy at least one of these three
priorities, listed in order of importance:
1. The first priority is preserving the integrity of the sport, one that incorporates
the elements of fun, cooperation, courtesy, and competition. This priority pays
homage to those who developed the sport in 1965 and those who have written
and approved rule changes over the years.
2. The second priority is what is collectively best for the players. This priority
examines rule changes for improving the player’s experience. It “tests”
suggested rule changes from the standpoint of minimizing player
disagreements, making it easier to learn the sport, teach the sport, and play
the sport, while also allowing for moderate innovation as player skills and
equipment develop and evolve.
3. The third priority is what is best for officiating. It “tests” rule changes to make it
less likely conflicts will occur between players as well as between players and
officials.
Guiding Principles
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook contains a wide variety of rules that cover the
court and equipment, recreational and social play as well as tournament play,
officiated and non-officiated. The following are Guiding Principles for those writing
and approving rules. To the extent possible, rules should:
1. Apply to all levels and categories of players: recreational and social players, as
well as professional and amateur tournament players (officiated and non-
officiated). Specific rules for a single category of player, for example, the pro
level player, should be approved after careful consideration and examination
of how the rule change might impact the sport beyond the pro level of
competition.
2. Be written with a deterministic focus, i.e., from the standpoint of “if this occurs,
this is what happens.” If something is not allowed or should not happen, the
consequences (for example: replay, fault, technical warning, etc.) should be
provided as part of the rule (e.g., replay, fault, technical warning, etc.).
3. Center on that which should not occur, not on what is permitted or allowed.
Attempts to include rules describing what is allowed will result in an
unnecessarily lengthy Rulebook.
4. Avoid ambiguity, player discretion, or referee judgment-related rules. Such
rules invite disagreements and different interpretations. To this end, when a
key word is used to describe when a rule applies, the word should be defined
as either a part of the rule or in the Definition section of the Rulebook.
5. Allow equipment manufacturers to innovate, as long as such innovation does
not overwhelm or outpace the average player’s ability to keep up with the
speed and difficulty of the sport. Equipment-related rule changes should be
given particularly close scrutiny because of their precedent-setting potential.
6. Have an element of precedent accorded to them. Change for change’s sake
should be avoided to avoid frustration among, or a loss of confidence by,
players.
7. Allow for an appropriate degree of player innovation. Such innovation should
maintain a healthy balance between historical rules that have been
instrumental to the sport’s growth and appeal.
8. Preserve the unique features and rules of the sport involving the Non-Volley
Zone and the two-bounce rule and prevent one shot, one paddle, or one type
of play from dominating the sport.
9. Address a known issue or anticipate trends and needs of the sport before
problems develop.
10. Be subjected to reviews and comments by domestic and international
stakeholders.

Underlying Principles
Pickleball is a game that requires cooperation and courtesy. A sense of fair
play by giving the opponent the benefit of any doubt is essential in
maintaining the game’s underlying principles of fun and competition.
• All points played are treated the same regardless of their importance: the
first point of the match is as important as match point.
• Either partner in doubles can make calls, especially line calls.
• Calls are made promptly to preserve fair play and prevent players from
making delayed calls for their own advantage.
• Players strive to cooperate when confronted with a situation not covered
by the Rulebook. Resolutions can be made by asking for a referee to
resolve a dispute. allowing the rally to stand, or in extreme cases, a replay
of the rally.
• Where possible, rules accommodate players with various adaptive needs.
• Players avoid wearing clothing that closely matches the ball color.
• Players should not question or comment on an opponent’s call except
through an appeal to a referee.

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Withdrawal, Retirement, or Forfeit
rows.content:
15.B.4.a Withdrawal, Retirement, or Forfeit. When a singles
player or doubles team withdraws, retires, or is
forfeited from a round robin event, then that player’s
or team’s match results will not count toward the
standings of that event and the player or team will not
be eligible to participate in any elimination playoff or
medal match for that event. The match results will
count towards the player’s or team’s rating.

rows.content:

or more teams only).

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Fourth Tie-Breaker
rows.content:
15.B.4.e Fourth Tie-Breaker. The fourth tie-breaker is the best
point differential of games played against the singles
player or doubles team with the next -highest number
of matches won. (For example, when players or teams
are tied for second-place, the total point differential
against the first-place singles player or doubles team is
used.)

3. PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
3.1. All League players must have a signed/accepted waiver with LWR PC and have a valid
LWR PC membership. To sign up, go to https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup/.
3.2. All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be found at:
https://www.dupr.com/.

the LWR PC membership: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB
3.4. Players are assigned to a community based on their primary address at the start of the
season.
3.5. Players may form teams with members from other communities; however, they are not
permitted to play for another community’s team if their own community already has a
team in their division and has roster availability for additional players.

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Second Tie-Breaker
rows.content:
15.B.4.c Second Tie-Breaker. The second tie-breaker is the
best point differential of all games played. This tie-
breaker does not apply across multiple pools where
the number of teams in each pool is not equal. (For
example, Team A wins their first match, 11-8, 11-4, so
they would have a point differential of +10. Team A
then wins the second match, 11-9, 2-11, 11-6. For the
second round, they would have a point differential of -
2. This would give them a total for the two rounds of
+8.)

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Third Tie-Breaker
rows.content:
15.B.4.d Third Tie-Breaker. The third tie-breaker is the best
point differential of head-to-head games.

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Fifth Tie-Breaker
rows.content:
15.B.4.f Fifth Tie-Breaker. The fifth tie-breaker is the highest
number of points scored across all matches in the
round robin. This tie-breaker does not apply across
multiple pools where the number of teams in each
pool is not equal.

Viewing Your Play History
My Play History lets a player review their recorded league match results and performance
across the league.
Use the Play History Scope list to choose which results to view:
• All Seasons/All Teams
• A specific season, league, division, or team
The page updates immediately to show only results within the selected scope.
At the top, summary cards show:
• Games Played — the number of recorded match-line results in the selected scope.
• Wins — recorded individual line wins.
• Losses — recorded individual line losses.
• Other Category - Tracks non-counting personal games, such as forfeits and
Picklebreaker matches. Scores Pending — matches whose scores have not yet been
entered and posted.
Below the summary, each match shows the match date, teams, home/away status, season,
league, division, lines played, and available game scores. A match that still needs scoring is
clearly labeled Scores Not Entered rather than being shown as an unclear “Other” result.
Select More Player Details in the header to open a separate, scrollable details window. It
provides five additional groups of scope-specific information:
• Matches: wins, losses, and match win percentage.
• Games: individual game wins, losses, and game win percentage.
• Points: points earned, points against, and point differential percentage.
• Ratings: average recorded partner and opponent ratings, plus adjusted and overall
performance estimates.
• Last 5 Matchups: the player’s five most recent results, marked with W or L.
The details window is designed for mobile as well as desktop and can be closed without
changing the selected History Scope.

rows.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

Quick Start Guide
As a player, you can use the League Management System to view your team schedules,
standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings
Season DUPR ratings are displayed throughout the system. To learn how DUPR ratings are
calculated, visit this website: https://www.dupr.com/how-it-works. For questions about
how the Club uses DUPR ratings, which rating is used, or other DUPR-related topics, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

Logging Into the System
The League Management System is located at https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com. Enter
your email address and password to sign in.
• First-Time Users: Enter the email address associated with your Club Membership
and click Forgot Password. A setup or a password reset email will be sent from no-
reply@auth.lwrpickleballclub.com to create your password. If you aren't sure which
email address you used, contact info@lwrpickleballclub.com.
• Passkeys & Biometrics: To log in using a passkey or fingerprint, click the Passkey
/ Fingerprint button to sign in or set up the feature.

password at any time when you are logged in the system. Click the Change Password
button located in the top header of the initial dashboard screen. Note: this will only change
the password in this League Management System and not the Club Membership system.

rows.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
rows.content:
CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
Each League team must have a designated Captain. A Captain may also serve as Co-Captain on
another team and may captain a team in the opposite gender category. However, a person may not
captain more than one team within the same gender category. There can be up to two Co-Captains.
Community Team Captains and Co-Captains have “Captain” access to the League Management
System (LMS) at league.lwrpickleballclub.com to manage teams, rosters, schedules, scores, and
overall league information. (For general club details, visit the main website at lwrpickleballclub.com).
Captains are responsible for their team roster, each match date setup including reserving all home
courts, recording/validating scores and general team management. Club League Management is
available at any time for help with any questions or concerns. See last page for contact information.
Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to host their share
of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability, resulting in a balanced home-
and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot reserve enough courts for all its assigned
home match dates, additional matches may be scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to
provide any courts due to limitations within their community or facility will play all their scheduled
matches as away games.
All league players also have access to the LMS through their personal Player Dashboard, where they
can view their assigned teams, upcoming and completed matches, team rosters, and standings. It also
features a full personal play history and quick-click shortcuts to email team captains. Captains can
also switch to the Player Dashboard to see their personal league information.

Viewing Schedules
In the Captain Tools block, use Division Schedules to track season matches and rankings
along with the ability to see all current club leagues/divisions.

individual matches, and results.

view teams and standings in other active club divisions.

rows.content:
MISSION STATEMENT
• Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club (LWR PC) mission aims to be the premier club in
Lakewood Ranch (LWR) and Southwest Florida.
• LWR PC’s goal is to foster fair, competitive and social play within LWR and area
communities and with local players.
• LWR PC's DUPR Leagues will provide an organized and competitive play that considers the
needs of Captains and Players, adheres to rules, and maintains low costs.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
rows.heading: VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
rows.content:
VIEW SCHEDULE/GAME INFORMATION
o On the Captain Dashboard, the selected team’s “next match” will be displayed along with
options for that match.
o Match Setup & Lineups: Captains must enter their lineups before match day to verify player
and team ratings. For complete details, see the Team/Game Rules in the DUPR League Rules.
o Completed Matches: Scroll down to the Recent results section to review score details for
past matches. Click on a match to see all detailed results including players and individual game
scores.
o Court Reservations & Match Details: The home team captain must reserve the required
number of courts for warm-ups and match play. You should confirm the start time and share all
location details with the visiting captain beforehand by clicking the Email Opposing Captains
button.
o Finding Captain Contact Info: Click the Division Captains button in the Captain Tools block
to view or print contact details for all captains and co-captains in your division.
o League Communication: For scheduling issues or other league questions, contact the league
managers by clicking the Contact League (email icon) button at the top of the screen.
o Match Balls & Score Sheets: The home team captain must bring league-provided balls to the
match and record all scores on a printed Match Score Sheet. Keep these physical score sheets
on file for the remainder of the season.

Upcoming Matches
Your Next Match appears at the top of the Captain Dashboard. From this section, captains
can view match details, email the opposing captains, print Match Score Sheet and enter final
scores. If this is a “flex league” you are also able to modify the match date/time and notify
opposing captains.
You can also manage your match lineup and score sheets here:
• Match Setup block: The Match Setup button turns red if your team hasn't entered
its lineup yet, and blue once you have. The system will email you a reminder to
complete this a few days before the actual match.
• Print Match Score Sheet button: Stays red until both teams complete their Match
Setup, turning green and ready to print once both lineups are in.
The Upcoming matches & byes section shows all upcoming match details, scheduling
information, and setup status. You can also click on a match for all available tools/options
for that match.

rows.content:
Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club (LWR PC)
Official Code of Conduct & Ethics
The Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club (LWR PC) is committed to a culture of competitive
fairness, integrity, and mutual respect. This Code applies to all members, team captains,
and guests during any LWR PC-sanctioned league play, tournament, or event.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
rows.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
rows.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

Quick Start Guide
As a Captain, use the League Management System to view schedules, manage rosters, see
division standings, check match details, and find other Captains' contact info. From the
upcoming match details screens, you can set your lineup, print score sheets, and enter or
validate match scores. If you manage multiple teams, a tab for each team will appear in your
My Teams section.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.

of the screen.

1. CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
1.1. Club main website: https://lwrpickleballclub.com
1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.
1.4. Each season consists of a multi-week regular play followed by championships/playoƯs.
1.5. League teams are divided by Divisions based on DUPR ratings.
1.6. The Leagues consist of:
1.6.1. Weekday DUPR League – Gender doubles scheduled play during the week
1.6.2. Saturday League - Gender Doubles/Mixed play using the Picklebreaker™ format
(every other Saturday)
1.6.3. PrimeTime League – Gender doubles, aged 65+ scheduled play on Fridays

2. CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAINS
Each team in the League must be led by a designated Captain. That individual may also assume
the position of Co-Captain on a diƯerent team and can also serve as Captain for a team of the
opposite gender. However, an individual is not permitted to hold the role of Captain for more
than one team within the same gender category in a Division. A Captain or Co-Captain is not
required to be an active player on the team but may instead serve in a supportive capacity by
assisting with the responsibilities assigned to the Captain. For comprehensive “How to”
instructions for Captains, please consult the DUPR League Captains Guide.

5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

6.1.4. Scoring: Each win earns 1 point with 9 total possible match points per date.
6.1.5. Player Cap: Each player plays exactly 3 games to 15.
6.1.6. Teams may use two doubles teams if they inform their opponents in advance. If a
team lacks a third doubles team, they must forfeit those 3 games and points. In this
case, the community team with three teams will play against the other two.

6.1.8. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both teams
are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the
matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 4-4 tie.
6.1.9. Men’s/Women’s 9.1 Division: These divisions will initially be scheduled as a “flex
league” with matches initially scheduled for Fridays at noon but the Captains can
modify the match day/time (within 7 days).

6.1.9.3. Scoring: Each win earns 1 point (5 total possible match points per date). If
it’s a tie (2-2) after round robin, there would be a single game to 15 by 2 using
the Picklebreaker™ format with the winning team collecting 1 additional point.
If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 1-point bonus.
6.1.9.4. Player Cap: Each player plays 4 games with a possible 6+ games.

6.1.9.7. The Picklebreaker™ shall be played only when the match is tied 2–2
following completion of all preceding rounds. The Picklebreaker™ features the
designated doubles teams that participated in the preceding rounds, rotating
in accordance with the Picklebreaker™ Rotation Rules. The Picklebreaker™
shall consist of one game to 15 points, win by two (2), using Rally Scoring.
Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not reflect
on individual’s W/L record.

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

6.2.3. Match Day Format: (See table below)
6.2.3.1. All Games: Games to 15 using Rally Scoring* (win by 1). 1 point per win. Two
one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams
switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points. Visitors choose serve,
receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.
6.2.3.2. Men's Round Robin: 3 Men’s teams play Round Robin (from low to high,
Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.3. Women's Round Robin: 3 Women’s teams play Round Robin (from low to
high, Teams 4 to 6). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.
6.2.3.5. Picklebreaker™ Game (Only played if tie at the end of all previous rounds -
12-12): Features all the mixed teams that played in the Mixed rounds. This will

be one game to 25 win by 2 using Rally Scoring. The winning team collects 3
additional points. (If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 3-point
bonus.) Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not
reflect on individual’s W/L record.
Teams are numbered 1–3 for Men’s Doubles, 4–6 for Women’s Doubles, and 7–12 for Mixed
Doubles. These team numbers correspond directly to the Match Score Sheet printed from the system.
We highly recommend assigning higher team numbers to teams with higher combined skill levels and
ratings (for instance, Team 6 should have a higher combined DUPR rating than Team 4 in Women’s or
Team 12 should be a higher team rating than Team 7 in Mixed Doubles).

6.2.4. Scoring: A maximum of 27 total possible match points per date. This includes 24
possible points awarded during standard play, plus a 3-point bonus. If the match
ends in a tie after the mixed doubles division (12-12), a Picklebreaker will be played
to determine the winner of the 3 bonus points. If there is no tie, the leading team

rows.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
rows.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

rows.heading: The Game
rows.content:
Section 1 The Game
Pickleball is a paddle sport that combines elements of badminton, table
tennis, and tennis. It is played using a special perforated ball on a 20-foot
by 44-foot court with a tennis type net. The court is divided into right and
left service courts and a non-volley zone on each end of the net (Figure 3-1).
Pickleball can be played as singles or doubles.
In standard pickleball, the ball is served diagonally across the net to the
opposite service court on the opponent’s end, using an approved motion.
The ball is then hit back and forth across the net until a player fails to return
the ball in accordance with the rules.
Standard pickleball uses a scoring method where points are scored only
when the serving team wins the rally. The server alternates service courts
and continues to serve until they lose a rally (commit a fault). Typically, the
first player or team scoring 11 points and leading by at least a 2-point
margin wins the game.
Rally scoring has been provisionally approved as an option (Rule 14.A),
wherein a point is scored by the team that wins each rally. Mini-singles
(Rule 14.B) is a half-court variation of standard singles.
Unique Features
Two-Bounce Rule. After the serve, the receiver must allow the ball to
bounce before making their first return, and then the serving team must
allow the ball to bounce before making their first return.
Non-Volley Zone. The non-volley zone is the area of the court that
extends 7 feet from the net on each end of the court, within which a player
is not allowed to hit the ball out of the air before it bounces.
Wheelchair and Adaptive Play. Players using wheelchairs and players
having certain disabilities may allow the ball to bounce twice before
returning the ball. The first bounce must be in the court, but the second

Preface
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook is the organization’s most important product.
It is the foundational document for the sport of pickleball and should be treated
with the respect accorded the sport’s founders and those who have written and
approved rules over the years.
Writing rules that are objective, clear, and concise is difficult work. Because those
involved in writing and/or approving rules come from diverse backgrounds and
experiences, it is important to have rule writing priorities and guiding principles
that help provide a measure of consistency from year to year. The following
Rulebook Priorities and Guiding Principles were developed to guide rule writers and
approvers in their important work.
Priorities
The following three priorities should be considered “tests” for any suggested rule
change. Any suggested rule change should satisfy at least one of these three
priorities, listed in order of importance:
1. The first priority is preserving the integrity of the sport, one that incorporates
the elements of fun, cooperation, courtesy, and competition. This priority pays
homage to those who developed the sport in 1965 and those who have written
and approved rule changes over the years.
2. The second priority is what is collectively best for the players. This priority
examines rule changes for improving the player’s experience. It “tests”
suggested rule changes from the standpoint of minimizing player
disagreements, making it easier to learn the sport, teach the sport, and play
the sport, while also allowing for moderate innovation as player skills and
equipment develop and evolve.
3. The third priority is what is best for officiating. It “tests” rule changes to make it
less likely conflicts will occur between players as well as between players and
officials.
Guiding Principles
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook contains a wide variety of rules that cover the
court and equipment, recreational and social play as well as tournament play,
officiated and non-officiated. The following are Guiding Principles for those writing
and approving rules. To the extent possible, rules should:
1. Apply to all levels and categories of players: recreational and social players, as
well as professional and amateur tournament players (officiated and non-
officiated). Specific rules for a single category of player, for example, the pro
level player, should be approved after careful consideration and examination
of how the rule change might impact the sport beyond the pro level of
competition.
2. Be written with a deterministic focus, i.e., from the standpoint of “if this occurs,
this is what happens.” If something is not allowed or should not happen, the
consequences (for example: replay, fault, technical warning, etc.) should be
provided as part of the rule (e.g., replay, fault, technical warning, etc.).
3. Center on that which should not occur, not on what is permitted or allowed.
Attempts to include rules describing what is allowed will result in an
unnecessarily lengthy Rulebook.
4. Avoid ambiguity, player discretion, or referee judgment-related rules. Such
rules invite disagreements and different interpretations. To this end, when a
key word is used to describe when a rule applies, the word should be defined
as either a part of the rule or in the Definition section of the Rulebook.
5. Allow equipment manufacturers to innovate, as long as such innovation does
not overwhelm or outpace the average player’s ability to keep up with the
speed and difficulty of the sport. Equipment-related rule changes should be
given particularly close scrutiny because of their precedent-setting potential.
6. Have an element of precedent accorded to them. Change for change’s sake
should be avoided to avoid frustration among, or a loss of confidence by,
players.
7. Allow for an appropriate degree of player innovation. Such innovation should
maintain a healthy balance between historical rules that have been
instrumental to the sport’s growth and appeal.
8. Preserve the unique features and rules of the sport involving the Non-Volley
Zone and the two-bounce rule and prevent one shot, one paddle, or one type
of play from dominating the sport.
9. Address a known issue or anticipate trends and needs of the sport before
problems develop.
10. Be subjected to reviews and comments by domestic and international
stakeholders.

Playing Surface. The court and the area surrounding the court designated for
playing.
Profanity. Words, phrases, or gestures commonly considered to be vulgar or
inappropriate in public or around children. Typically included are words used as
expletives or verbal intensifiers.
Rally. Continuous play that occurs after the serve is hit and before the ball
becomes dead.
Receiver. The player who returns the serve.
Replay. The restart of a rally without the awarding of a point or changing of the
server.
Retirement. A singles player or doubles team’s decision to discontinue playing in
a match in progress.
Second Serve (Doubles). A term used to describe the serving condition after the
first server loses their serve.
Second Server (Doubles). The first server’s partner. The second server serves
after the first server loses serve.
Serve. The initial strike of the ball with the paddle to start a rally.
Server. The player who initiates a rally by serving the ball.
Service Court. The area of the court on either side of the centerline, excluding the
non-volley zone. (See Rule 3.A.4.f for specifications.)
Serving Area. The area behind the baseline on each end of the court. (See Rule
3.A.4.g for specifications.)
Side Out. The awarding of the serve to the opposing team after a singles player or
doubles team loses its serve.
Starting Server (Doubles). For each doubles team, the player designated to
serve first at the start of a game.
Technical Foul. A one-point penalty assessed for extreme unsportsmanlike
actions or behaviors.
Technical Warning. A punitive warning assessed for minor unsportsmanlike
actions or behaviors.
Verbal Warning. A non-punitive caution for minor unsportsmanlike behavior,
usually given in advance of assessing a technical warning or technical foul for such

rows.heading: 9.B Faults — No Enforcement of Other Faults
rows.content:

has committed any type of fault other than a non-volley zone fault
or a service foot fault, they may mention the specific fault to the
opponent upon completion of the rally, but they have no authority
to enforce the fault. The final decision on fault resolution belongs
to the player that allegedly committed the fault.

rows.heading: 9.B Faults — Fault Occurrence

for non-volley zone violations involving momentum. (See Rule
11.A.2.)

rows.heading: Item on Court
rows.content:
10.J Item on Court. When anything that is worn or carried by a player lands on
the player’s end of the court (except when the item contacts the non-volley
zone as a result of the player volleying the ball (see Rule 11.A.1)), the ball
remains in play, even if the ball hits the item.

rows.heading: “Out” Ball
rows.content:
8.C “Out” Ball. A served ball that does not land in the correct service court on
the opponent’s end of the court, including one that lands on the non-volley
zone line, is “out.” Any other ball that lands outside the court is “out.”

Underlying Principles
Pickleball is a game that requires cooperation and courtesy. A sense of fair
play by giving the opponent the benefit of any doubt is essential in
maintaining the game’s underlying principles of fun and competition.
• All points played are treated the same regardless of their importance: the
first point of the match is as important as match point.
• Either partner in doubles can make calls, especially line calls.
• Calls are made promptly to preserve fair play and prevent players from
making delayed calls for their own advantage.
• Players strive to cooperate when confronted with a situation not covered
by the Rulebook. Resolutions can be made by asking for a referee to
resolve a dispute. allowing the rally to stand, or in extreme cases, a replay
of the rally.
• Where possible, rules accommodate players with various adaptive needs.
• Players avoid wearing clothing that closely matches the ball color.
• Players should not question or comment on an opponent’s call except
through an appeal to a referee.

rows.heading: Player Equipment or Apparel Problem
rows.content:
10.I Player Equipment or Apparel Problem. If a player experiences an
equipment or apparel problem during a rally, play must continue until the
end of the rally.

rows.heading: 18.B Apparel — Footwear

opponent’s end of the court while the ball is live.

equipment and apparel between rallies as long as the flow of the game is not
adversely impacted.

The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams

rows.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
rows.content:
CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
Each League team must have a designated Captain. A Captain may also serve as Co-Captain on
another team and may captain a team in the opposite gender category. However, a person may not
captain more than one team within the same gender category. There can be up to two Co-Captains.
Community Team Captains and Co-Captains have “Captain” access to the League Management
System (LMS) at league.lwrpickleballclub.com to manage teams, rosters, schedules, scores, and
overall league information. (For general club details, visit the main website at lwrpickleballclub.com).
Captains are responsible for their team roster, each match date setup including reserving all home
courts, recording/validating scores and general team management. Club League Management is
available at any time for help with any questions or concerns. See last page for contact information.
Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to host their share
of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability, resulting in a balanced home-
and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot reserve enough courts for all its assigned
home match dates, additional matches may be scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to
provide any courts due to limitations within their community or facility will play all their scheduled
matches as away games.
All league players also have access to the LMS through their personal Player Dashboard, where they
can view their assigned teams, upcoming and completed matches, team rosters, and standings. It also
features a full personal play history and quick-click shortcuts to email team captains. Captains can
also switch to the Player Dashboard to see their personal league information.

Profile Button
To access additional system settings, click the round profile icon near the top right of your
mobile screen (or to the right of your name on desktops). This opens the Profile popup
window, where you can manage the following options:
• Change Password / Passkey: Open the password update window or set up passkey
access for faster sign-ins.
• Change Picture: This will change the profile icon to your picture. This is only
available when you are on the Player Dashboard.
• Dashboard Appearance: Toggle sidebar menu themes (dark or light), collapse the
sidebar and adjust dashboard section headers. Note: Appearance settings are saved
individually per device.
• Club Website Link: Jump directly to the main club membership portal to manage
account renewals or payments.
• Logging Out: Once you have completed your tasks, please log out of the system.
Note that logging out will only end your active session on your current device and
browser.

25.A.7 Propelling Wheelchair with Foot. A player who is unable to
propel their wheelchair with one or both upper extremities
(arms) for the entire duration of a match is permitted to propel
the wheelchair using a single foot against the ground. The player
is then subject to the following restrictions for the entire
duration of the match:
1) The player must not utilize their upper extremities for
propulsion.
2) The player’s foot must not be in contact with the ground
when the player strikes the ball to make a shot.
3) The player’s lower extremities must not contact any
wheelchair wheel.

wheelchair for the duration of an entire match are permitted to
utilize wheelchairs powered by electric motors. Power
wheelchairs must be controlled by the player only and cannot
exceed 10 miles-per-hour.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
rows.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
rows.content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
rows.heading: Weather Issues
rows.content:
6.2.7. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both teams
are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the
matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 13-13 tie.
6.2.8. Snacks/Drinks: Optional; the Home Team may provide them if desired.
6.2.9. Jamboree: held at the end of the season.

rows.heading: 19.G No Definitive Call by Referee — No Call by Referee – With Line Judges
rows.content:
19.G.3 No Call by Referee – With Line Judges. When the referee is
unable to make a call upon appeal, the line judge’s call stands.

rows.heading: No Definitive Call by Referee
rows.content:
19.G No Definitive Call by Referee. When the referee is unable to make a call
upon appeal, the outcome of the rally is determined by Rules 19.G.1
through 19.G.4.

rows.heading: 19.G No Definitive Call by Referee — No Call by Players and Referee – Without Line Judges
rows.content:
19.G.2 No Call by Players and Referee – Without Line Judges. Upon
appeal, when the players and the referee are unable to make a
call, the ball is ruled “in.”

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
rows.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

rows.content:
• Complete all required questions to set up your team. Most of the information you enter, such as
your Team Name, Captain, and other team details, can be changed later. This initial information
will be used to create and activate your team and associate it with the appropriate community and
related league information.

to enter your payment information or, if available, select your current payment method already on
file.

details, important next steps, and upcoming dates and deadlines.

during registration as the Captain and Co-Captain(s). Once this is completed, your initial team
registration and setup will be complete.

available for you to begin adding and managing your players.
My Play History Screen

Managing Team Rosters
To update your team roster, go to the Captain Tools section on your Captain Dashboard
and click Manage Roster to add, change, or remove players.
• Changing Captains or Co-Captains: On the Team Roster Management screen, click
Change Captain/Co-Captain next to your team name. This opens an email draft to
submit your request directly to League Management.
Team Roster Management Window

Player Dashboard Overview
The dashboard gives you quick access to your teams, upcoming matches, completed
matches, team standings, and your play history. If you are a member of multiple teams,
select the correct team under My Team in the sidebar to update the view.
Dashboard Highlights:
• Top Navigation: At the very top right of the Player Dashboard, you can access the
Player User Guide, email the league, or click the button next to your name to update
your profile, change your password, adjust appearance settings, or view your club
membership.
• Sidebar Options: Use the sidebar menu to switch between teams if you belong to
more than one, view your personal Play History, and check the Division Schedule
or Standings. Select League Documents to view all available files for your league.
• Team Information: The main dashboard gives you immediate access to your next
match, including buttons for match details and posted lineups. You can monitor your
team's rank, record, and your personal Season DUPR rating, as well as review
upcoming schedules and recent results.
• In the My Team section, click on any captain to send them an email, or select View
Team to see the complete player roster with DUPR ratings and individual records.
Player Dashboard Main Screen (Desktop view)

Entering Match Scores
Captains enter scores, record forfeits, and confirm official match results. When entering
scores, normally select the “Use this saved team” pulldown to display the previously
entered Match Setup team. If there were changes to that, simply select the correct player in
the individual player pulldown option.
• Game Forfeits & Retirements: Refer to the official League Rules when entering
results for individual games impacted by player or play-related issues.
• Full Match Cancellations: If an entire match date is forfeited or cannot be played
due to weather or scheduling conflicts, do not enter it into the system. Instead,
contact League Management at info@lwrpickleballclub.com.
• Eligible/Ineligible Player: In actual score entry, the same eligibility rules apply to
the players entered for each game line. An ineligible player cannot be selected, and
score fields are blocked if that line has an eligibility issue.
Enter Match Scores Screen

Player Dashboard Main Screen (Mobile view)
The mobile version includes two unique navigation areas not found on desktop:
• Top Menu: Click or tap the “hamburger” (☰) icon to open the main navigation
menu. From there, you can switch between teams, view your play history, check
division schedules and standings, or access the latest league documents.
• Top Navigation: Switch your Dashboard view (if you are also a captain) or change
your Active Team (if you are a member of multiple teams).
• Bottom Navigation: Quickly access key menu items via a shortcut bar at the bottom
of the screen.

email to validate or dispute the entry.
 Alternate Entry: By mutual agreement before the match, the visiting team may enter
scores first, leaving the home team to validate them.

right of any LMS screen) for details regarding using rosters, scoring and the general use of the

Captain Dashboard Overview
Use the dashboard to overall manage your team(s), keep on top of all upcoming and prior
matches, manage rosters, view standings, and handle score tasks. If you captain multiple
teams, select the correct team under My Team in the sidebar to update the view.
Dashboard Highlights:
• Top Navigation: At the very top right of the Captain Dashboard, you can access the
Captain User Guide, email the league, or click the button next to your name to
update your profile, change your password, adjust appearance settings, or view your
club membership.

league.

your division schedules and division captain contacts.
• Team Information: Your main dashboard gives you quick access to your next
match—complete with quick-action buttons for match setup. You can also monitor
your team's current rank, record, and any pending score entry or validations,
alongside quick-view sections for division standings, upcoming schedules, and
recent match results.
Main Captain Dashboard Screen (Desktop View)

Upcoming Matches
Your Next Match appears at the top of the Captain Dashboard. From this section, captains
can view match details, email the opposing captains, print Match Score Sheet and enter final
scores. If this is a “flex league” you are also able to modify the match date/time and notify
opposing captains.
You can also manage your match lineup and score sheets here:
• Match Setup block: The Match Setup button turns red if your team hasn't entered
its lineup yet, and blue once you have. The system will email you a reminder to
complete this a few days before the actual match.
• Print Match Score Sheet button: Stays red until both teams complete their Match
Setup, turning green and ready to print once both lineups are in.
The Upcoming matches & byes section shows all upcoming match details, scheduling
information, and setup status. You can also click on a match for all available tools/options
for that match.
Upcoming / Unverified Matches Screen

rows.heading: 20.J Officiating Decision Challenge — Rescinding Challenge Request
rows.content:
20.J.1 Rescinding Challenge Request. After a request for the Head
Referee or Tournament Director has been acknowledged by the
referee, the player may rescind the request; however, the player
or team will be charged a standard time-out. When a standard
time-out is not available, the referee will assess a technical foul
against the player or team.

rows.heading: 15.A Event Categories. — Gender Events
rows.content:
15.A.1 Gender Events. In events categorized by gender, only members of
that gender are allowed to play in that event.

Viewing Your Team Roster
Select View Team from the "My Team" block to see your complete roster.
This section displays:
• Full list of current team members
• Individual player ratings and season records
• Player contact information
Viewing Division Standings
The Division Standings section shows rankings, records, and point differentials for your
selected team. You can also view other teams in your division by using the drop-down menu
in the header.
To access the standings:
• Sidebar: Click Division Standings.
• Dashboard: Click the Division Rank block located right under your next scheduled
match.
• Mobile Shortcut: Tap the Standings icon in the bottom navigation bar.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
rows.heading: ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
rows.content:
 Entering Match Scores: To enter scores, click the Enter Match Scores button in the
match. This option becomes available only on or after the scheduled match date and
will be red.
 Forfeits and Weather Delays: If an entire match date is forfeited or canceled due to
weather, notify League Management. They will log the information for that match and
update the standings.
 Score Entry Process: When entering scores, use the dropdown menus to select the
players for each game (built from your Match Setup), then enter the scores in each
game block. Click Submit when finished; the system will check for errors before saving.
 Score Verification: Once scores are submitted, the opposing captain will receive an
email request to verify them, and a red notification count will appear in their Pending
Match Verifications block. The opposing captain must open the match, review the
scores, and click the verification button (or dispute button if they don’t accept the
scores as written). Both captains will then be notified, and the standings will update
automatically.
o The visiting team captain must verify match scores promptly. This ensures there is enough time
to review the results and enter them into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

rows.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Invalid Medical Time-Out Request – No Time-Out
rows.content:
22.D.6 Invalid Medical Time-Out Request – No Time-Out. Requesting
a medical time-out when no valid medical condition exists and a
standard time-out is not available to be charged. See Rule
21.C.10.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: Replay – Net System Malfunction
rows.content:
13.J Replay – Net System Malfunction. When a net system malfunctions during
a rally, the rally must be replayed.

rows.heading: 23.B Withdrawal from Bracket — Ineligibility to Continue Play
rows.content:
23.B.3 Ineligibility to Continue Play. A singles player or doubles team
that withdraws is removed from all upcoming matches in the
specified bracket.

Quick Start Guide
As a Captain, use the League Management System to view schedules, manage rosters, see
division standings, check match details, and find other Captains' contact info. From the
upcoming match details screens, you can set your lineup, print score sheets, and enter or
validate match scores. If you manage multiple teams, a tab for each team will appear in your
My Teams section.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop

rows.heading: 18.C Starting Server Identification (Doubles) — Match Forfeit – Refusal to Wear Identification
rows.content:
18.C.1 Match Forfeit – Refusal to Wear Identification. When a player
refuses to wear the required form of identification, the
Tournament Director may impose a forfeit of the player’s match.

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Withdrawal, Retirement, or Forfeit
rows.content:
15.B.4.a Withdrawal, Retirement, or Forfeit. When a singles
player or doubles team withdraws, retires, or is
forfeited from a round robin event, then that player’s
or team’s match results will not count toward the
standings of that event and the player or team will not
be eligible to participate in any elimination playoff or
medal match for that event. The match results will
count towards the player’s or team’s rating.

rows.heading: Retirements and Withdrawals
rows.content: Section 23 Retirements and Withdrawals

Main Captain Dashboard Screen (Mobile View)
The mobile version includes two unique navigation areas not found on desktop:
• Top Menu: Click or tap the “hamburger” (☰) icon to open the main navigation
menu. From there, you can switch between teams, go to your Captain tools or access
the latest league documents.
• Top Navigation: Switch your Dashboard view (from/to Captain/Player) or change
your Active Team (if you captain multiple teams).
• Bottom Navigation: Quickly access key menu items via a shortcut bar at the bottom
of the screen.

Quick Start Guide
As a player, you can use the League Management System to view your team schedules,
standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings
Season DUPR ratings are displayed throughout the system. To learn how DUPR ratings are
calculated, visit this website: https://www.dupr.com/how-it-works. For questions about
how the Club uses DUPR ratings, which rating is used, or other DUPR-related topics, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

player and click Add Player to Team. League Management will automatically be

rows.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered Before Match Starts
rows.content:
18.A.1 Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered Before Match Starts. Before
a match starts, when a player is discovered using a paddle that is
not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List or is not in
compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D, the player
must switch to a compliant paddle. There is no penalty to switch
paddles.

rows.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered After Match Concludes
rows.content:
18.A.3 Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered After Match Concludes. After
a match has ended, when a player is discovered to have used a
paddle that is not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List
or is not in compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D,
the match results stand.

rows.heading: 18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle — Match Forfeit – Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered During Play.
rows.content:
18.A.2 Match Forfeit – Non-Compliant Paddle Discovered During Play.
During a match, when a player is discovered playing with a paddle
that is not listed on the USA Pickleball Approved Paddle List or is
not in compliance with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D, a
match forfeit will be imposed on the player.

rows.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Dangerous Paddle or Ball Abuse
rows.content:

When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

rows.heading: 22.L Ejection or Expulsion — Injurious Paddle or Ball Abuse
rows.content:
22.L.2 Injurious Paddle or Ball Abuse. Damage to the venue or injury
to a player, official, or spectator through an act of paddle or ball
abuse or other acts of physical violence.

rows.heading: Damaged Ball
rows.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: Ball Around Net Post

post.

rows.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball

broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

o The registration fee is per team, per division, per season, as announced before the season

rows.heading: Damaged Ball
rows.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

rows.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Construction
rows.content:
3.C.5 Construction. The ball must be made of durable material molded
with a smooth surface and free of texturing. The ball may have a
slight ridge at the seam, as long as it does not significantly impact
the ball’s flight characteristics. (See Figure 3-2.)
The ball with larger holes is customarily used
for indoor play (pictured on the left). The ball
with smaller holes is customarily used for
outdoor play (pictured on the right).
Figure 3-2: Approved Balls – Examples

rows.heading: 24.B Extra Ball — Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls
rows.content:
24.B.1 Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls. When an extra ball
carried by a player is visible to an opponent or falls to the
playing surface while the ball is live, it is a fault against the
player.

rows.heading: Returned Ball Placement
rows.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side
rows.content:
13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side. When a ball bounces in the
court on the receiving player’s end of the net and then returns to
the opponent’s side of the net without being hit, the receiving
player may cross over, under, or around the net to hit the ball, but
only after the ball has first crossed back to the opponent’s end of
the net.

rows.heading: 7.B Ball Release — No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release
rows.content:
7.B.2 No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release. Some natural rotation of
the ball is expected during any release of the ball. The server must
not manipulate the ball to add spin with any part of the server's
body or the paddle prior to hitting the ball to make the serve,
except that the server may allow the ball to roll off the face of the
paddle by gravity. Spin may be applied to the ball upon contact by
the paddle.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — After Hitting the Ball
rows.content:
13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball. A player may cross the plane of the net
immediately after hitting the ball. The allowance to cross the plane
of the net only applies while executing the current strike of the ball
and for continuation associated with the current strike of the ball.

rows.heading: Ball Selection
rows.content:
16.G Ball Selection. The Tournament Director will choose the tournament ball
from the official list of approved balls posted on the USA Pickleball website.

rows.heading: Ball Specifications
rows.content:
3.C Ball Specifications. The requirements for the ball are set forth in Rules 3.C.1
through 3.C.5. The complete list of approved balls is posted on the USA
Pickleball website.

rows.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
rows.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

rows.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
rows.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: Ball Contacting Net
rows.content:
13.A Ball Contacting Net. When the ball contacts the net, or the rope or cable at
the top of the net between the net posts, the ball remains in play.

rows.heading: Damaged Ball
rows.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
rows.content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
rows.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

rows.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
rows.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

rows.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Ball Abuse
rows.content:
22.D.2 Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly throwing or hitting a dead
ball in frustration or anger with negligent disregard for the
consequences as long as the ball does not strike a person but
puts a person at risk or in danger.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: Ball Crossing Plane of Net
rows.content:
13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net. A ball must entirely cross to a player’s end of
the net before the player hits the ball.

rows.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
rows.content:
10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

rows.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Ball Release Not Visible
rows.content:
20.E.2.a Replay – Ball Release Not Visible. When it is
questionable whether the release of the ball was not
visible to the referee and receiver, the referee may
call for a replay. When the referee is certain that the
release of the ball was not visible, the referee must
call for a replay.

rows.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
rows.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

rows.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
rows.content:
20.E.2.i Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

rows.heading: “In” Ball
rows.content:
8.B “In” Ball. A served ball that clears the opponent’s non-volley zone line and
lands in the correct service court is “in.” A ball returned by a player that
lands on the opponent’s end of the court is “in.”

rows.heading: “Out” Ball
rows.content:
8.C “Out” Ball. A served ball that does not land in the correct service court on
the opponent’s end of the court, including one that lands on the non-volley
zone line, is “out.” Any other ball that lands outside the court is “out.”

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: 13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side — Fault – Ball Not Contacted
rows.content:
13.I.2.b Fault – Ball Not Contacted. When a ball bounces in
the court on the receiving player’s end of the net and
then returns to the opponent’s end of the net without
being hit, it is a fault against a player who fails to hit
the ball before it bounces once on the opponent’s end
of the net.

rows.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Ball Height.
rows.content:
20.E.2.h Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Ball Height.
When it is questionable whether the ball was no
higher than the server’s waist when the paddle
contacted the ball to make a volley serve, the referee
may call for a replay.

rows.heading: Extra Ball
rows.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

rows.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing
rows.content:
10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: 13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side — Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Ball
rows.content:
13.I.2.a Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Ball
Crosses. When a ball bounces in the court on the
receiving player’s end of the net and is returning to the
opponent’s end without being hit, it is a fault against
the player if the player crosses the plane of the net
before the ball crosses entirely.

rows.section_label: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
rows.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System
rows.content:
13.B.1 Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System. When a player serves a
ball that contacts the net support system on either end of the net
or returns a ball that contacts the net support system before going
