Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
rows.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
rows.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
rows.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
rows.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

rows.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Double Elimination
rows.content:
15.B.1 Double Elimination. In a double elimination format, after losing
one match, a singles player or doubles team plays in a consolation
bracket. The player or team is eliminated from competition after
one loss in the consolation bracket. The winner of the consolation
bracket plays the winner of the winners’ bracket to determine first
place and second place. If the winner of the consolation bracket
defeats the winner of the winners’ bracket, then a tie-breaker
match to 15 points must be played to determine first place and
second place. The loser of the final match in the consolation
bracket wins third place.

rows.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Double Elimination
rows.content:
15.B.1 Double Elimination. In a double elimination format, after losing
one match, a singles player or doubles team plays in a consolation
bracket. The player or team is eliminated from competition after
one loss in the consolation bracket. The winner of the consolation
bracket plays the winner of the winners’ bracket to determine first
place and second place. If the winner of the consolation bracket
defeats the winner of the winners’ bracket, then a tie-breaker
match to 15 points must be played to determine first place and
second place. The loser of the final match in the consolation
bracket wins third place.

rows.heading: The Game
rows.content:
Section 1 The Game
Pickleball is a paddle sport that combines elements of badminton, table
tennis, and tennis. It is played using a special perforated ball on a 20-foot
by 44-foot court with a tennis type net. The court is divided into right and
left service courts and a non-volley zone on each end of the net (Figure 3-1).
Pickleball can be played as singles or doubles.
In standard pickleball, the ball is served diagonally across the net to the
opposite service court on the opponent’s end, using an approved motion.
The ball is then hit back and forth across the net until a player fails to return
the ball in accordance with the rules.
Standard pickleball uses a scoring method where points are scored only
when the serving team wins the rally. The server alternates service courts
and continues to serve until they lose a rally (commit a fault). Typically, the
first player or team scoring 11 points and leading by at least a 2-point
margin wins the game.
Rally scoring has been provisionally approved as an option (Rule 14.A),
wherein a point is scored by the team that wins each rally. Mini-singles
(Rule 14.B) is a half-court variation of standard singles.
Unique Features
Two-Bounce Rule. After the serve, the receiver must allow the ball to
bounce before making their first return, and then the serving team must
allow the ball to bounce before making their first return.
Non-Volley Zone. The non-volley zone is the area of the court that
extends 7 feet from the net on each end of the court, within which a player
is not allowed to hit the ball out of the air before it bounces.
Wheelchair and Adaptive Play. Players using wheelchairs and players
having certain disabilities may allow the ball to bounce twice before
returning the ball. The first bounce must be in the court, but the second

Underlying Principles
Pickleball is a game that requires cooperation and courtesy. A sense of fair
play by giving the opponent the benefit of any doubt is essential in
maintaining the game’s underlying principles of fun and competition.
• All points played are treated the same regardless of their importance: the
first point of the match is as important as match point.
• Either partner in doubles can make calls, especially line calls.
• Calls are made promptly to preserve fair play and prevent players from
making delayed calls for their own advantage.
• Players strive to cooperate when confronted with a situation not covered
by the Rulebook. Resolutions can be made by asking for a referee to
resolve a dispute. allowing the rally to stand, or in extreme cases, a replay
of the rally.
• Where possible, rules accommodate players with various adaptive needs.
• Players avoid wearing clothing that closely matches the ball color.
• Players should not question or comment on an opponent’s call except
through an appeal to a referee.

rows.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
rows.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:

1. CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
1.1. Club main website: https://lwrpickleballclub.com
1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.
1.4. Each season consists of a multi-week regular play followed by championships/playoƯs.
1.5. League teams are divided by Divisions based on DUPR ratings.
1.6. The Leagues consist of:
1.6.1. Weekday DUPR League – Gender doubles scheduled play during the week
1.6.2. Saturday League - Gender Doubles/Mixed play using the Picklebreaker™ format
(every other Saturday)
1.6.3. PrimeTime League – Gender doubles, aged 65+ scheduled play on Fridays

5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

6.1.1. Scheduling: Games are typically scheduled for Wednesdays at noon for women
and Thursdays at noon for men. DUPR 9: See 6.1.9 below.
6.1.2. Roster & Courts: 6 Players / 3 Lines. Requires 3 courts.
6.1.3. Match Format: Round robin; one game to 15, win by 1. Each team receives two
one-minute timeouts. Teams switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points,
and visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3.

6.1.8. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both teams
are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the
matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 4-4 tie.
6.1.9. Men’s/Women’s 9.1 Division: These divisions will initially be scheduled as a “flex
league” with matches initially scheduled for Fridays at noon but the Captains can
modify the match day/time (within 7 days).

6.1.9.1. This division will only have 2 lines (4 players) and require 2 courts.
6.1.9.2. Match Format: Teams play Round Robin. 2 out of 3 to 11 (win by 2). Plus,
potential Picklebreaker™ to 15. Teams will switch ends before Game 2. If a
third game is required, teams will switch ends during Game 3 when the first
team reaches six (6) points. Visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in
game 1 and 3. Each team receives one one-minute timeout/game.

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

6.2.3. Match Day Format: (See table below)
6.2.3.1. All Games: Games to 15 using Rally Scoring* (win by 1). 1 point per win. Two
one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams
switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points. Visitors choose serve,
receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.
6.2.3.2. Men's Round Robin: 3 Men’s teams play Round Robin (from low to high,
Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.3. Women's Round Robin: 3 Women’s teams play Round Robin (from low to
high, Teams 4 to 6). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.
6.2.3.5. Picklebreaker™ Game (Only played if tie at the end of all previous rounds -
12-12): Features all the mixed teams that played in the Mixed rounds. This will

be one game to 25 win by 2 using Rally Scoring. The winning team collects 3
additional points. (If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 3-point
bonus.) Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not
reflect on individual’s W/L record.
Teams are numbered 1–3 for Men’s Doubles, 4–6 for Women’s Doubles, and 7–12 for Mixed
Doubles. These team numbers correspond directly to the Match Score Sheet printed from the system.
We highly recommend assigning higher team numbers to teams with higher combined skill levels and
ratings (for instance, Team 6 should have a higher combined DUPR rating than Team 4 in Women’s or
Team 12 should be a higher team rating than Team 7 in Mixed Doubles).

The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want

rows.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Double Elimination
rows.content:
15.B.1 Double Elimination. In a double elimination format, after losing
one match, a singles player or doubles team plays in a consolation
bracket. The player or team is eliminated from competition after
one loss in the consolation bracket. The winner of the consolation
bracket plays the winner of the winners’ bracket to determine first
place and second place. If the winner of the consolation bracket
defeats the winner of the winners’ bracket, then a tie-breaker
match to 15 points must be played to determine first place and
second place. The loser of the final match in the consolation
bracket wins third place.

rows.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Non-Pool Play
rows.content:
15.B.6 Non-Pool Play. After playing a round robin to determine seeding,
seeded singles players or doubles teams play a single-elimination
or double-elimination playoff, using a match format of two of three
games to 11 points, one game to 15 points, or one game to 21
points, all win by two points.

rows.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Single Elimination with Consolation
rows.content:
15.B.2 Single Elimination with Consolation. In a single elimination with
consolation format, after losing one match, a singles player or
doubles team plays in a consolation bracket. The player or team is
eliminated from competition after one loss in the consolation
bracket. The final two players or teams in the winners’ bracket play
for first place and second place. The final two singles players or
doubles teams in the consolation bracket play for third place.

rows.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
rows.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

5.14.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.14.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.14.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.
5.14.4. Captains will form teams following regular season rules and Season DUPR ratings.
5.14.5. Players may participate in a Division end-of-season/Championship game only if
they have competed in at least one game within that Division during the current
regular season.
5.14.6. A round-robin format will be implemented instead of traditional matchups: players
in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.
5.14.7. Every win earns one point, and overall points determine Gold, Silver, and Bronze
team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.
5.14.8. All Championship Day games will be posted to DUPR but not recorded in the LMS.
5.14.9. Gold / 1st place division teams are named the Season’s Division Champions based
on Championship Day results, not regular-season standings alone.

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

5.14.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.14.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.14.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.
5.14.4. Captains will form teams following regular season rules and Season DUPR ratings.
5.14.5. Players may participate in a Division end-of-season/Championship game only if
they have competed in at least one game within that Division during the current
regular season.
5.14.6. A round-robin format will be implemented instead of traditional matchups: players
in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.
5.14.7. Every win earns one point, and overall points determine Gold, Silver, and Bronze
team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.
5.14.8. All Championship Day games will be posted to DUPR but not recorded in the LMS.
5.14.9. Gold / 1st place division teams are named the Season’s Division Champions based
on Championship Day results, not regular-season standings alone.

structuralContext.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

Rated) are eligible to participate in any division. However, it is strongly recommended that
a Certified DUPR Coach or qualified pickleball professional provide input to help
determine the player's most appropriate skill level. The team captain is ultimately
responsible for ensuring the player is placed in the proper division to promote balanced
and fair competition for all teams.

5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

5.4. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

5.5. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.

5.7. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.7.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.7.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.7.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.

5.8. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between
games. Coaches and non-players must always remain oƯ the court; only active players
may be on the courts.
5.9. Spectator Interference: Spectators/non-participants must not be consulted on any call,
nor shall they influence any calls or decisions on the court.

5.12. Makeup Game Deadline: All makeup games must be played at least one week before the
playoƯs/championship date.

5.13. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.13.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.13.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).
5.13.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.

6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

6.1.1. Scheduling: Games are typically scheduled for Wednesdays at noon for women
and Thursdays at noon for men. DUPR 9: See 6.1.9 below.
6.1.2. Roster & Courts: 6 Players / 3 Lines. Requires 3 courts.
6.1.3. Match Format: Round robin; one game to 15, win by 1. Each team receives two
one-minute timeouts. Teams switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points,
and visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3.

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

6.2.1. Scheduling: Games are typically scheduled for every other Saturday at noon.
6.2.2. Roster & Courts: 12 players—6 men and 6 women—divided into six teams: 3 men’s
doubles teams and 3 women’s doubles teams. Mixed teams may be formed from
the gender doubles players or can be from additional players who participate only in

rows.heading: Standard Time-Out
rows.content:
21.A Standard Time-Out. Two standard time-outs are allowed per singles
player or doubles team for each 11-point and 15-point game and three
time-outs for a 21-point game.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Number Available
rows.content:
21.C.3 Number Available. A player may be granted only one medical
time-out per match.

rows.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Between Games
rows.content:
21.A.3 Between Games. Between games, players may request to use
one or both standard time-outs before the start of the next
game. The players must inform the referee. The standard time-
out will start immediately after the expiration of the time-out
between games. A time-out must be charged when any portion
of the time is used. When the requesting singles player or
doubles team is ready to resume play before a requested time-
out begins, that time-out is not charged.

rows.heading: Time Between Matches
rows.content:
21.G Time Between Matches. The allowed time between matches, including a
tie-breaker match to determine a championship, is 10 minutes. When all
players agree, a match may start early.

rows.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Duration
rows.content:
21.F.1 Duration. A maximum of two minutes is allowed to change ends
between games.

rows.heading: Use of Time-Outs Between Games
rows.content:
24.E Use of Time-Outs Between Games. Players must notify the opponent of
their intent to use one or both standard time-outs before the start of the
next game. (Modifies Rule 21.A.3)

rows.heading: End Change Time-Out
rows.content:
21.B End Change Time-Out. The referee will call a time-out to allow players to
change ends at specified points during single-game matches and tie-
breaker games. Players will not change ends during the tie-breaker game
when the first game of the match was forfeited due to late arrival.
21.B.1 11-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 11
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 6.
21.B.2 15-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 15
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 8.
21.B.3 21-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 21
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 11.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Valid Medical Condition
rows.content:
21.C.8 Valid Medical Condition. When medical personnel, or the
Tournament Director, when medical personnel are not available,
determine that a valid medical condition exists, the player must
be able to resume play in 15 minutes or less. When the player is
able to resume play in fewer than 15 minutes, the remaining
medical time is lost and no longer available to the player during
the match.

rows.heading: 21.B End Change Time-Out — Duration
rows.content:
21.B.5 Duration. A maximum of one minute is allowed to change ends
during a game.

rows.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Time-Outs
rows.content:
17.D.15 Time-Outs. Enforce time-out procedures. (See Section 21.)
17.D.16 15-Second Warnings. Announce when there are 15 seconds
remaining in a time-out. At the end of the 15 seconds, the referee
must call “time in” and then the score when all players are ready
to play or should be ready to play.

rows.heading: Extending Time to Report to Match
rows.content:
16.M Extending Time to Report to Match. The Tournament Director may allow
an extension of time for players to report to a match when circumstances
warrant.

rows.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Change of Starting Server
rows.content:
21.F.3 Change of Starting Server. Teams may change the starting
server between games and should notify the referee before the
start of the next game.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Between Games
rows.content:
21.C.2 Between Games. Between games, a player may request a
medical time-out, when available, before the start of the next
game.

rows.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — After Medical Time-Out
rows.content:
21.A.4 After Medical Time-Out. A player may use available standard
time-outs after the expiration of a medical time-out.

rows.heading: Referee Time-Out
rows.content:
21.D Referee Time-Out. The referee may call a referee time-out to address
extenuating circumstances that require an extended interruption of play
and summon assistance, as necessary. When designated personnel are
not available, the Tournament Director will respond. Extenuating
circumstances include, but are not limited to, those cited in this section.

rows.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Requesting Time-Out
rows.content:
21.A.2 Requesting Time-Out. Any player may call a time-out between
rallies before the next serve occurs or between games. The time-
out must be called audibly by voice or visibly by hand signal, or
both, and must be directed toward the opposing player or team
and to the referee.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Time Start
rows.content:
21.C.7 Time Start. When medical assistance arrives, the referee will
start a 15-minute timer. Play must resume as soon as possible
but no later than 15 minutes of elapsed time.

rows.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Before Start of Match
rows.content:
21.A.1 Before Start of Match. A standard time-out cannot be called
before a match starts.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Match Retirement
rows.content:
21.C.9 Match Retirement. A match retirement is imposed when a
player is not able to continue play after the 15-minute medical
time-out period expires. A player may use their available
standard time-outs to allow more time before the match must
be retired (Rule 21.A.4). In doubles, if the retiring player's partner
decides to continue, the match will resume following all
applicable rules. The retiring player must leave the playing
surface.

rows.heading: Medical Time-Out
rows.content:
21.C Medical Time-Out. A player needing medical attention during a match,
including between games, may request a medical time-out.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Rescinding Medical Time-Out Request
rows.content:
21.C.4 Rescinding Medical Time-Out Request. If the player rescinds
the medical time-out after the medical personnel have been
called and before they have arrived, a standard time-out will be
charged and the medical time-out will not be charged. When a
standard time-out is not available, the referee will assess a
technical foul against the player or team for delay of game.

rows.heading: Time-Out Between Games
rows.content:
21.F Time-Out Between Games. The referee will call a time-out between
games of a match.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Duration
rows.content:
21.C.6 Duration. A maximum of 15 minutes is allowed for a medical
time-out. However, when medical treatment is rendered off-
court at another location at the venue, the time to transport the
player to and from the off-court location will be excluded from
15-minute time period.

rows.heading: 21.D Referee Time-Out — Resuming Play
rows.content:
21.D.4 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

rows.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Resuming Play
rows.content:
21.F.4 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

rows.content:
21.E.2 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

rows.heading: 21.B End Change Time-Out — Resuming Play
rows.content:
21.B.8 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

player or doubles team for each 11-point and 15-point game and three
time-outs for a 21-point game.

rows.content:
5.5. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will

rows.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Between Games
rows.content:
21.A.3 Between Games. Between games, players may request to use
one or both standard time-outs before the start of the next
game. The players must inform the referee. The standard time-
out will start immediately after the expiration of the time-out
between games. A time-out must be charged when any portion
of the time is used. When the requesting singles player or
doubles team is ready to resume play before a requested time-
out begins, that time-out is not charged.

rows.heading: Time Between Matches

tie-breaker match to determine a championship, is 10 minutes. When all
players agree, a match may start early.

between games.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
rows.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
rows.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

rows.heading: End Change Time-Out
rows.content:
21.B End Change Time-Out. The referee will call a time-out to allow players to
change ends at specified points during single-game matches and tie-
breaker games. Players will not change ends during the tie-breaker game
when the first game of the match was forfeited due to late arrival.
21.B.1 11-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 11
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 6.
21.B.2 15-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 15
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 8.
21.B.3 21-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 21
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 11.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Valid Medical Condition
rows.content:
21.C.8 Valid Medical Condition. When medical personnel, or the
Tournament Director, when medical personnel are not available,
determine that a valid medical condition exists, the player must
be able to resume play in 15 minutes or less. When the player is
able to resume play in fewer than 15 minutes, the remaining
medical time is lost and no longer available to the player during
the match.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
rows.heading: Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages
rows.content:
5.13. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.13.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.13.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).
5.13.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
rows.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
rows.content:
CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
Each League team must have a designated Captain. A Captain may also serve as Co-Captain on
another team and may captain a team in the opposite gender category. However, a person may not
captain more than one team within the same gender category. There can be up to two Co-Captains.
Community Team Captains and Co-Captains have “Captain” access to the League Management
System (LMS) at league.lwrpickleballclub.com to manage teams, rosters, schedules, scores, and
overall league information. (For general club details, visit the main website at lwrpickleballclub.com).
Captains are responsible for their team roster, each match date setup including reserving all home
courts, recording/validating scores and general team management. Club League Management is
available at any time for help with any questions or concerns. See last page for contact information.
Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to host their share
of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability, resulting in a balanced home-
and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot reserve enough courts for all its assigned
home match dates, additional matches may be scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to
provide any courts due to limitations within their community or facility will play all their scheduled
matches as away games.
All league players also have access to the LMS through their personal Player Dashboard, where they
can view their assigned teams, upcoming and completed matches, team rosters, and standings. It also
features a full personal play history and quick-click shortcuts to email team captains. Captains can
also switch to the Player Dashboard to see their personal league information.

rows.heading: 21.B End Change Time-Out — Duration
rows.content:
21.B.5 Duration. A maximum of one minute is allowed to change ends
during a game.

rows.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Time-Outs
rows.content:
17.D.15 Time-Outs. Enforce time-out procedures. (See Section 21.)
17.D.16 15-Second Warnings. Announce when there are 15 seconds
remaining in a time-out. At the end of the 15 seconds, the referee
must call “time in” and then the score when all players are ready
to play or should be ready to play.

rows.heading: Extending Time to Report to Match
rows.content:
16.M Extending Time to Report to Match. The Tournament Director may allow
an extension of time for players to report to a match when circumstances
warrant.

rows.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Change of Starting Server
rows.content:
21.F.3 Change of Starting Server. Teams may change the starting
server between games and should notify the referee before the
start of the next game.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Between Games
rows.content:
21.C.2 Between Games. Between games, a player may request a
medical time-out, when available, before the start of the next
game.

rows.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — After Medical Time-Out
rows.content:
21.A.4 After Medical Time-Out. A player may use available standard
time-outs after the expiration of a medical time-out.

5.8. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between

rows.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Before Start of Match

21.A.1 Before Start of Match. A standard time-out cannot be called

rows.heading: Match Setup and Roster Exchange
rows.content:
5.4. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

structuralContext.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

Rated) are eligible to participate in any division. However, it is strongly recommended that
a Certified DUPR Coach or qualified pickleball professional provide input to help
determine the player's most appropriate skill level. The team captain is ultimately
responsible for ensuring the player is placed in the proper division to promote balanced
and fair competition for all teams.

5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

5.4. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.

5.5. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.

5.7. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.7.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.7.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.7.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.

5.8. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between
games. Coaches and non-players must always remain oƯ the court; only active players
may be on the courts.
5.9. Spectator Interference: Spectators/non-participants must not be consulted on any call,
nor shall they influence any calls or decisions on the court.

5.12. Makeup Game Deadline: All makeup games must be played at least one week before the
playoƯs/championship date.

5.13. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.13.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.13.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).
5.13.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.

6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

6.1.1. Scheduling: Games are typically scheduled for Wednesdays at noon for women
and Thursdays at noon for men. DUPR 9: See 6.1.9 below.
6.1.2. Roster & Courts: 6 Players / 3 Lines. Requires 3 courts.
6.1.3. Match Format: Round robin; one game to 15, win by 1. Each team receives two
one-minute timeouts. Teams switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points,
and visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3.

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

6.2.1. Scheduling: Games are typically scheduled for every other Saturday at noon.
6.2.2. Roster & Courts: 12 players—6 men and 6 women—divided into six teams: 3 men’s
doubles teams and 3 women’s doubles teams. Mixed teams may be formed from
the gender doubles players or can be from additional players who participate only in
the mixed round. Requires 4 courts.

6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams
representing each squad, and any tied team match is decided by the exciting Picklebreaker
format. PrimeTime emphasizes spirited competition, sportsmanship, and the opportunity
for experienced players to continue enjoying high-quality league play in a community-
focused environment.

play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.13.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.

remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).

o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

rows.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
rows.content:
CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
Each League team must have a designated Captain. A Captain may also serve as Co-Captain on
another team and may captain a team in the opposite gender category. However, a person may not
captain more than one team within the same gender category. There can be up to two Co-Captains.
Community Team Captains and Co-Captains have “Captain” access to the League Management
System (LMS) at league.lwrpickleballclub.com to manage teams, rosters, schedules, scores, and
overall league information. (For general club details, visit the main website at lwrpickleballclub.com).
Captains are responsible for their team roster, each match date setup including reserving all home
courts, recording/validating scores and general team management. Club League Management is
available at any time for help with any questions or concerns. See last page for contact information.
Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to host their share
of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability, resulting in a balanced home-
and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot reserve enough courts for all its assigned
home match dates, additional matches may be scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to
provide any courts due to limitations within their community or facility will play all their scheduled
matches as away games.
All league players also have access to the LMS through their personal Player Dashboard, where they
can view their assigned teams, upcoming and completed matches, team rosters, and standings. It also
features a full personal play history and quick-click shortcuts to email team captains. Captains can
also switch to the Player Dashboard to see their personal league information.

rows.document_title: LWR Pickleball Club Code of Conduct
rows.content:
1. Standard of Play & Sportsmanship
• Golden Rule: Treat every player, regardless of skill level, with the same respect you
expect to receive.
• Positive Environment: Support your partners and remain respectful to your
opponents. Avoid "trash talk" that crosses the line into being mean-spirited or
discouraging.
• Integrity of the Game: Players must make line calls that are "clear and certain." In
accordance with standard pickleball officiating, all "close" calls must be resolved in
favor of the opponent.
• Player Integrity: Any attempt to manipulate ratings through "sandbagging,"
reporting false scores, or intentionally losing matches is strictly prohibited and
grounds for immediate expulsion.
• On-Court Decorum: Profanity, paddle throwing, or aggressive physical gestures
toward opponents, partners, or spectators will not be tolerated.

are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the
matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 4-4 tie.
6.1.9. Men’s/Women’s 9.1 Division: These divisions will initially be scheduled as a “flex
league” with matches initially scheduled for Fridays at noon but the Captains can
modify the match day/time (within 7 days).

6.1.9.1. This division will only have 2 lines (4 players) and require 2 courts.
6.1.9.2. Match Format: Teams play Round Robin. 2 out of 3 to 11 (win by 2). Plus,
potential Picklebreaker™ to 15. Teams will switch ends before Game 2. If a
third game is required, teams will switch ends during Game 3 when the first
team reaches six (6) points. Visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in
game 1 and 3. Each team receives one one-minute timeout/game.

6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

6.2.3. Match Day Format: (See table below)
6.2.3.1. All Games: Games to 15 using Rally Scoring* (win by 1). 1 point per win. Two
one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams
switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points. Visitors choose serve,
receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.
6.2.3.2. Men's Round Robin: 3 Men’s teams play Round Robin (from low to high,
Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.3. Women's Round Robin: 3 Women’s teams play Round Robin (from low to
high, Teams 4 to 6). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.

12-12): Features all the mixed teams that played in the Mixed rounds. This will

be one game to 25 win by 2 using Rally Scoring. The winning team collects 3
additional points. (If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 3-point
bonus.) Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not
reflect on individual’s W/L record.
Teams are numbered 1–3 for Men’s Doubles, 4–6 for Women’s Doubles, and 7–12 for Mixed
Doubles. These team numbers correspond directly to the Match Score Sheet printed from the system.
We highly recommend assigning higher team numbers to teams with higher combined skill levels and
ratings (for instance, Team 6 should have a higher combined DUPR rating than Team 4 in Women’s or
Team 12 should be a higher team rating than Team 7 in Mixed Doubles).

rows.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
rows.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

rows.content:
15.B.4.c Second Tie-Breaker. The second tie-breaker is the
best point differential of all games played. This tie-
breaker does not apply across multiple pools where
the number of teams in each pool is not equal. (For
example, Team A wins their first match, 11-8, 11-4, so
they would have a point differential of +10. Team A
then wins the second match, 11-9, 2-11, 11-6. For the
second round, they would have a point differential of -
2. This would give them a total for the two rounds of
+8.)

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Fourth Tie-Breaker

point differential of games played against the singles
player or doubles team with the next -highest number
of matches won. (For example, when players or teams
are tied for second-place, the total point differential
against the first-place singles player or doubles team is
used.)

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Third Tie-Breaker
rows.content:

point differential of head-to-head games.

rows.heading: Standard Time-Out
rows.content:
21.A Standard Time-Out. Two standard time-outs are allowed per singles
player or doubles team for each 11-point and 15-point game and three
time-outs for a 21-point game.

rows.heading: End Change Time-Out
rows.content:
21.B End Change Time-Out. The referee will call a time-out to allow players to
change ends at specified points during single-game matches and tie-
breaker games. Players will not change ends during the tie-breaker game
when the first game of the match was forfeited due to late arrival.
21.B.1 11-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 11
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 6.
21.B.2 15-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 15
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 8.
21.B.3 21-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 21
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 11.

rows.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Number Available
rows.content:
21.C.3 Number Available. A player may be granted only one medical
time-out per match.

rows.heading: 21.B End Change Time-Out — Duration
rows.content:
21.B.5 Duration. A maximum of one minute is allowed to change ends
during a game.

rows.heading: Time Between Matches
rows.content:
21.G Time Between Matches. The allowed time between matches, including a
tie-breaker match to determine a championship, is 10 minutes. When all
players agree, a match may start early.

rows.heading: Time-Outs and Breaks
rows.content: Section 21 Time-Outs and Breaks

rows.heading: Use of Time-Outs Between Games
rows.content:
24.E Use of Time-Outs Between Games. Players must notify the opponent of
their intent to use one or both standard time-outs before the start of the
next game. (Modifies Rule 21.A.3)

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — First Tie-Breaker
rows.content:
15.B.4.b First Tie-Breaker. The first tie-breaker is the best
record of head-to-head matches among the tied
teams.

rows.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Duration
rows.content:
21.F.1 Duration. A maximum of two minutes is allowed to change ends
between games.

rows.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Time-Outs
rows.content:
17.D.15 Time-Outs. Enforce time-out procedures. (See Section 21.)
17.D.16 15-Second Warnings. Announce when there are 15 seconds
remaining in a time-out. At the end of the 15 seconds, the referee
must call “time in” and then the score when all players are ready
to play or should be ready to play.

then wins the second match, 11-9, 2-11, 11-6. For the
second round, they would have a point differential of -
2. This would give them a total for the two rounds of
+8.)

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Fourth Tie-Breaker
rows.content:

point differential of games played against the singles
player or doubles team with the next -highest number
of matches won. (For example, when players or teams
are tied for second-place, the total point differential
against the first-place singles player or doubles team is
used.)

rows.heading: 15.B.4 Round Robin — Third Tie-Breaker
rows.content:
15.B.4.d Third Tie-Breaker. The third tie-breaker is the best
point differential of head-to-head games.

5.14. End of Season PlayoƯs/Championship Day (All Leagues)
5.14.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.14.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.14.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.

regular season.

in Line 1 will compete against all other players in Line 1, and similarly, players in
additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.

team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.

1. CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
1.1. Club main website: https://lwrpickleballclub.com
1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.
1.4. Each season consists of a multi-week regular play followed by championships/playoƯs.
1.5. League teams are divided by Divisions based on DUPR ratings.
1.6. The Leagues consist of:
1.6.1. Weekday DUPR League – Gender doubles scheduled play during the week
1.6.2. Saturday League - Gender Doubles/Mixed play using the Picklebreaker™ format
(every other Saturday)
1.6.3. PrimeTime League – Gender doubles, aged 65+ scheduled play on Fridays

4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

Rated) are eligible to participate in any division. However, it is strongly recommended that
a Certified DUPR Coach or qualified pickleball professional provide input to help
determine the player's most appropriate skill level. The team captain is ultimately
responsible for ensuring the player is placed in the proper division to promote balanced
and fair competition for all teams.

5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.

5.13. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.13.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.13.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).
5.13.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.

5.14.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These

date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and

additional lines will compete against all other players in their respective lines.
5.14.7. Every win earns one point, and overall points determine Gold, Silver, and Bronze
team winners. Ties are broken by regular season standings; the higher seed
wins.
